Key bugs: parse_u64 sets out=0 first, violating "out unchanged on failure" (e.g. "12x" or empty). Also overflow: wraps mod 2^64, accepts values > UINT64_MAX (e.g. "18446744052737044961" wraps to something). Also empty string accepted (contract says nonempty). Also leading zeros allowed — fine. Also parse_u64 marked noexcept but returns false — fine, no exception.

Registry: get returns string_view into vector; concurrent add may push_back causing reallocation/remove of element → dangling view; also vector growth invalidates. Also get with no bounds check — but contract violation? get(i) out of range → UB. Also readers retain values after get returns while writers add: string_view may dangle if vector reallocates or string moved? add moves string into vector; existing strings not moved, but reallocation copies them to new buffer → old views dangle. Also get returns view while lock released; add push_back can reallocate → dangling. Fix: store shared_ptr or use deque of unique_ptr / return std::string by value, or use std::vector<std::unique_ptr<std::string>> to keep addresses stable.
